claims.text: The bursary provides up to £250.
The bursary helps cover transport, accommodation, and reasonable expenses for a specific research-related trip.
Applications close on Monday 14 September at midday BST.
Applicants must be Members of ERBA.
The bursary needs to be used to support a specific trip, such as visiting a gallery, museum, collection, site, or meeting someone important to research.
The bursary can be used to attend an event directly related to research.
The bursary cannot be used to cover attendance fees or membership costs.
Eligible costs include standard class travel, mileage at 45p per mile, local travel, accommodation (typically not more than £120 per night), and reasonable expenses (not more than £60 per full day).
The funding needs to be used between November 2026 and April 2027.
The bursary can be used as part-funding towards a trip.
Access requirement costs are covered separately and do not need to be included in the application.
Applicants need to outline likely costs in their application.
Applications will be reviewed and scored by members of the Paul Mellon Centre (PMC) team and the ERBA Convenor.
Bursary holders must provide a brief report (up to five hundred words) after their trip detailing how they used the funding and sharing any learning or observations.
Bursary holders do not need to provide receipts or detailed accounts unless requested.
Bursary holders may be asked to contribute to future ERBA mailing or web content.
Applications are submitted through a specific form.

claims.text: Grants are available for research and dissemination projects.
The grants are for projects in British art, visual culture, and architectural history.
Grant applications for the Autumn 2026 round are open.
The application deadline is Monday 14 September at 11:59pm BST.
There is a new grant of up to £40,000 for organizations undertaking ambitious and sustained research in British art, visual culture, and architectural history.
This £40,000 grant is designed primarily to support staff costs for research projects with public-facing outcomes and/or legacy.
Outcomes for the £40,000 grant could include exhibitions, digital projects, catalogues, or similar dissemination forms.
Grants of up to £6,000 are available to support individuals disseminating research on British art through publications like monographs, edited collections, catalogues, and articles.
This £6,000 grant can support practical publishing costs, such as image copyright fees.
Grants of up to £6,000 are available to support organizations producing publications related to their exhibitions and displays.
This £6,000 grant can support practical publishing costs, such as image and production costs.
Grants of up to £5,000 are available to support organizations digitizing their collections to make them freely available online.
This £5,000 grant can support personnel costs and equipment for digitization projects.
Grants of up to £3,000 are available to support organizations disseminating research on British art through events (live, online, hybrid).
This £3,000 grant can support costs such as venue hire, accommodation for speakers, and staffing for events.
Grants of up to £25,000 are available to help protect and preserve significant works of British art through conservation research.
This £25,000 grant can support staff costs and equipment for conservation research projects.
General application guidance, FAQs, and information on funding focus are available.
Information about previously successful projects and people is available.
Contact information for the Grants team is provided via email.
